desc: Fault 205 candidate root cause (see evidence/2026-10-29-gravitylinux-survey.md). 5012 found a secondaries-only write denial over a physical range near the ADT end but read only the legacy CTRR_A/B regs. M4 has a second CTRR instance, CTRR_C (s3_0_c11_c0_0/1, EL1 encodings), enabled on secondaries only; Asahi m1n1 a735ea2+442c7a2+00b8814 and Gravity eb6cab7 reserve it as an FDT mem-rsv, which with idle=nop+arm64.nowfxt makes M4/M4 Pro SMP reliable (Gravity runs all 16 CPUs on M4 Max). Step 1 offline: add the CTRR_C/D/CTXR names from Asahi 442c7a2 to our proxyclient apple_regs.json and t6040-cpu-sysreg-diff.py; cherry-pick a735ea2+00b8814 into the m1n1 fork (keep From: authors). Step 2 rig, reads only: dump CTRR_C/D LWR/UPR/CTL per core and overlay on the 5012 v3 AT bitmap (Asahi says 48 KiB; 5012 saw >256 KiB, explain the gap). Step 3 rig: 217 cow reproducer at maxcpus=2 then 6 with the reservation m1n1; PASS = no 205 fault over the run matrix. Do not drop maxcpus=1 from the daily image until 4000 matrix passes. UPDATE 2026-10-30 (evidence/2026-10-30-t6040-5015-ctrr-macos-abstract-and-live-layout.md): macOS writes no CTRR reg on any CPU, so the window is firmware-locked and a carve-out is the only remedy; macOS reads [3,0,11,1,2/3] with UPR inclusive (last byte UPR+0xfff), so Asahi ALIGN_UP(UPR) is a page short when UPR is aligned. Live boot: m1n1 80badc91 has no CTRR mem-rsv; [adt_end, m1n1 _base) = 384 KiB of allocatable RAM covers 5012s denial. Step 2 now reads [3,0,11,0,0..3], [3,0,11,1,0..5] on the boot CPU AND one secondary, UPR inclusive, overlaid on [adt_end-16K, adt_end+0x60000). Step 3 runs two variants: (a) the Asahi series as-is, (b) a Wallace m1n1 mem-rsv over [adt_end, m1n1 _base); both cmdlines add arm64.nowfxt (CPU has FEAT_WFxT; flokli-code.patch with idle=nop skips WFIT but __delay still loops on WFET). CORRECTION 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex 5495c18): variant (b) reserves the FIXED span [adt_end, adt_end+0x60000), using m1n1 _base only if it equals adt_end+0x60000 (else warn and keep the fixed span), because after a chainload the running stage can sit elsewhere. UPR: if its low 12 bits are zero, the exclusive end = UPR+0x1000 rounded up to 16K and Asahi ALIGN_UP is a page short; if UPR ends in 0xfff, Asahi is right; record which case. Step 3 pass criterion: log any fault OUTSIDE the reserved span (the 2026-07-29 maxcpus=14 boot faulted again about 7.9 MiB above adt_end); one means a second mechanism. The no-IMPDEF/TLBI finding covers the early boot text only. CENSUS 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex ac71e08): no CTRR self-write anywhere in the macOS kernel, no s3_0_c15 (chicken) writes; the per-CPU-init caveat is closed except whether SPRR/GXF state differs between boot CPU and secondaries (only relevant if step 3 still faults). BLOCKER for steps 1 and 3: the enrolled m1n1 source 80badc91 is not on GitHub (NEXT_STEPS manual command 2b). HYPOTHESIS 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex 782a58c, unverified, needs the ADT): the July-29 second fault (PA 0x10006724f90, adt_end+0x7d8f90, outside the 384 KiB carve-out) could be a preloaded firmware-protected range (ANE segment-ranges or similar for other coprocessors) that Linux was allowed to allocate, rather than CTRR_C. Counterpoint: today the kernel CMA sits at 0x10005000000..0x10006ffffff, which would contain that PA on a similar layout, so it may just be a cascade page. Once the ADT is available, compare every segment-ranges or pre-loaded region with that PA and with live /proc/iomem; any such range that is not reserved is a bug on its own. PARITY 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex 83c6870; only if 205 survives the reservation): macOS starts a secondary with plain 32-bit writes to PMGR reg[0]+0x88000: +0x4 = packed mask of started cores, +0x8+4*c = per-cluster core mask for every cluster (0 for clusters not started), stop = +0x0; entry PA 0, no reset-vector write, no readback, only dsb sy x2 before, and no protection state anywhere in the path. The +0x4 bit position comes from the PMGR ADT clusters table (u16 ncores, u16 bitpos per cluster). m1n1 main (16b1f61, src/smp.c:161/164; CHECK 80badc91 once pushed) writes +0x4 = 1 << (4*cluster + core) and +0x8+4*cluster = 1 << core (a single core, not a running mask). On J614s (4E+5P+5P, live DT cpu@0..3, cpu@10100..10104, cpu@10200..10204) cluster 1 core 4 (bit 8) aliases cluster 2 core 0 (bit 8). All 14 cores start, so this is not a start failure and not a known 205 mechanism; compare with the ADT clusters table. Per-CPU sysregs XNU sets on every secondary start/wake that m1n1 leaves alone or sets differently: s3_4_c15_c14_6 (AGTCNTRDIR_EL12) = 3 (m1n1 0); ACTLR_EL1 bits [11:9] cleared; s3_4_c15_c9_6 |= (index<<4)|0xf (timebase event stream, unset by m1n1). Parity only; none looks like memory protection. CORRECTIONS 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex 28d50d9): the s3_0_c11 census is 18 guest (_EL12) encodings, not 20 (conclusion unchanged). The per-cluster mask vs one-core-per-start difference at +0x8+4*c is equivalent under write-1-to-act; the only parity item is the +0x4 bit-8 collision.
